## Question

"Nigeria is getting worse" is one number, and nothing in it says where. Which states got worse, and which months were deadliest?

## Claim

<figure class="portrait-inline">
<img src="nyanya-buses-2014.jpg" alt="Burnt-out red buses at Nyanya bus station, Abuja, their windows gone and debris across the ground.">
<figcaption>Nyanya bus station, Abuja, after the 2014 bombing. VOA / Wikimedia Commons, public domain</figcaption>
</figure>

The headline is true. 29,300 events and 94,586 deaths, 2015 to 2025 (data). A national rate of +22.9 per cent a year (model).

It is also the least useful number in the file.

## Counter-claim

Two facts a national average cannot carry.

The state with the most deaths is not the state worsening fastest (model). And a deadlier month is not a busier one (data).

## Setup

One row per state, LGA, year and month: 772 cells, 37 states, 2015 to 2026 (data). The analysis fits 2015 to 2025. 2026 is six months and still being revised, so it sits out.

Every number is tagged: **(data)** counted in the file, **(model)** fitted, **(proof)** arithmetic.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| output: false
source("analysis.R")

pal <- c(worse = "#0f766e", flat = "#6b7280", deaths = "#b45309",
         events = "#0e7490", ink = "#57606a")
grid <- "#d7dce1"
```

## The analysis

### Thirty-seven speeds, one direction

The national rate is the middle of a wide spread. State trends run from +1.5 to +59.8 per cent a year (model), a standard deviation of 14.5 points (model). Thirty-three states are worse than flat. Four are flat, and none improves (model).

Sokoto leads at +59.8 per cent (model). Its toll in eleven years is 2,372 deaths (data). Borno's is 35,355 (data).

```{r}
#| label: fig-trend
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Thirty-seven speeds. Borno, the deadliest state, is fifth from the bottom."
#| fig-height: 6.9

tr <- trend[order(trend$pct), ]
tr$state <- factor(tr$state, levels = tr$state)
tr$col   <- ifelse(tr$worse, pal[["worse"]], pal[["flat"]])

fig1 <- plot_ly(data = tr, x = ~pct, y = ~state,
  type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
  marker = list(color = ~col, size = 7),
  error_x = list(type = "data", symmetric = FALSE,
    array = ~(high - pct), arrayminus = ~(pct - low),
    color = "#9aa4b2", thickness = 1.1, width = 0),
  hovertemplate = "%{y}: %{x:.1f}% a year<extra></extra>")

fig1 <- layout(fig1,
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 60, t = 30, b = 10),
  showlegend = FALSE,
  shapes = list(list(type = "line", yref = "paper", y0 = 0, y1 = 1,
    x0 = national_pct, x1 = national_pct,
    line = list(color = pal[["ink"]], width = 1, dash = "dot"))),
  annotations = list(
    list(x = national_pct, yref = "paper", y = 1.0, xanchor = "center",
      yanchor = "bottom", showarrow = FALSE,
      text = sprintf("country: +%.1f", national_pct),
      font = list(size = 12, color = pal[["ink"]])),
    list(x = borno$pct, y = "Borno", xanchor = "left", yanchor = "bottom",
      showarrow = FALSE, xshift = 8,
      text = "Borno", font = list(size = 12, color = pal[["deaths"]])),
    list(x = trend$pct[trend$state == "Sokoto"], y = "Sokoto",
      xanchor = "right", yanchor = "bottom", showarrow = FALSE, xshift = -8,
      text = "Sokoto", font = list(size = 12, color = pal[["deaths"]]))),
  xaxis = list(title = "events per year, 2015-2025 (% change a year)",
    gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 12)),
  yaxis = list(title = "", tickfont = list(size = 11), gridcolor = grid))

config(fig1, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: every interval but four sits right of zero; the spread is nearly the size of the national trend itself.*

### The deadliest state is not the fastest

Borno is +8.9 per cent a year (model), the third slowest in the country. It carries 30 per cent of all deaths since 2019 (data).

Rank the states by toll and by speed, and the lists barely overlap: rank correlation 0.21 (model). The fastest risers are small: Kwara has 430 deaths in eleven years (data), one-eightieth of Borno's.

```{r}
#| label: fig-speed-size
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Speed against size. The biggest risers are not the biggest tolls."
#| fig-height: 4.53

sc <- trend
sc$col <- ifelse(sc$state == "Borno", pal[["deaths"]],
                 ifelse(sc$worse, pal[["worse"]], pal[["flat"]]))
sc$show <- sc$state %in% c("Borno", "Sokoto", "Zamfara", "Katsina", "Benue")

fig2 <- plot_ly(data = sc, x = ~deaths15_25, y = ~pct, type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers", marker = list(color = ~col, size = 10, opacity = 0.85),
  text = ~state, hovertemplate = "%{text}<br>%{x:,.0f} deaths, %{y:.1f}% a year<extra></extra>")

fig2 <- layout(fig2,
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 30, t = 30, b = 10),
  showlegend = FALSE,
  shapes = list(list(type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1,
    y0 = national_pct, y1 = national_pct,
    line = list(color = pal[["ink"]], width = 1, dash = "dot"))),
  annotations = c(
    unname(lapply(seq_len(sum(sc$show)), function(i) {
      s <- sc[sc$show, ][i, ]
      list(x = s$deaths15_25, y = s$pct, text = s$state, showarrow = FALSE,
        xshift = 0, yshift = 14, font = list(size = 11, color = s$col))
    })),
    list(list(xref = "paper", x = 0.02, y = 0.96, showarrow = FALSE,
      xanchor = "left", text = sprintf("rank correlation %.2f", rho_level),
      font = list(size = 12, color = pal[["ink"]])))),
  xaxis = list(title = "deaths, 2015-2025 (log scale)", type = "log",
    gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 12)),
  yaxis = list(title = "events per year (% change)", gridcolor = grid,
    zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 12)))

config(fig2, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: Borno sits far right and low; the high points sit left. Bigger is not faster.*

### Ten of the twelve deadliest months are Borno

The top twelve state-months by deaths, 2019 to 2025, are overwhelmingly one state: ten are Borno, and they hold 84 per cent of those deaths (data).

The exception is the point of the chart. Niger, March 2022: 491 deaths from 28 events (data), 17.5 per event, against Borno's 5 to 12. One LGA, Mariga, took 302 of them in five events (data).

Across states, events and deaths rank together at 0.86 (data). Events and deaths per event rank at 0.39 (data). Busy and lethal are not the same list.

```{r}
#| label: fig-months
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Twelve deadliest state-months. Ten are Borno; the exception is a single month in Niger."
#| fig-height: 5.06

tm <- top12[order(top12$pv_fatalities), ]
tm$label <- factor(tm$label, levels = tm$label)
tm$col <- ifelse(tm$state == "Borno", pal[["deaths"]], pal[["events"]])

fig3 <- plot_ly(data = tm, x = ~pv_fatalities, y = ~label, type = "bar",
  orientation = "h", marker = list(color = ~col),
  text = ~sprintf("%s events", comma(pv_events)), textposition = "outside",
  textfont = list(size = 11, color = pal[["ink"]]),
  hovertemplate = "%{y}: %{x:,.0f} deaths<extra></extra>")

fig3 <- layout(fig3, bargap = 0.35,
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 70, t = 30, b = 10),
  xaxis = list(title = "deaths in the month", gridcolor = grid,
    zeroline = FALSE, range = c(0, 760), tickfont = list(size = 12)),
  yaxis = list(title = "", tickfont = list(size = 12), gridcolor = grid),
  annotations = list(list(x = outlier$pv_fatalities, y = outlier$label,
    text = sprintf("%.1f deaths per event", outlier$pv_fatalities / outlier$pv_events),
    showarrow = TRUE, ax = 60, ay = -18, xanchor = "left",
    font = list(size = 11, color = pal[["events"]]))))

config(fig3, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: one colour fills ten rows. The odd row is not a big month; it is a lethal one.*

### Deaths have a season; events do not

Events by calendar month are flat: 288 to 320 a month, on average, across equal years (data). Deaths are not. January to June average 891 deaths a month-year; July to October, 700 (data). Ratio 1.27, on the same years.

Both series are indexed to their own mean, so the shapes compare directly (proof).

```{r}
#| label: fig-season
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Deaths rise in the first half; events are a flat line."
#| fig-height: 4.31

sv <- seas_m
sv$deaths_i <- 100 * sv$deaths_pm / mean(sv$deaths_pm)
sv$events_i <- 100 * sv$events_pm / mean(sv$events_pm)

fig4 <- plot_ly(data = sv, x = ~m, y = ~deaths_i, type = "bar",
  name = "deaths", marker = list(color = pal[["deaths"]], opacity = 0.75),
  hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y:.0f}<extra>deaths</extra>")
fig4 <- add_trace(fig4, x = ~m, y = ~events_i, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers",
  name = "events", line = list(color = pal[["events"]], width = 2.5),
  marker = list(color = pal[["events"]], size = 8),
  hovertemplate = "%{x}: %{y:.0f}<extra>events</extra>")
fig4 <- layout(fig4, barmode = "overlay",
  margin = list(l = 10, r = 30, t = 30, b = 10),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.15, font = list(size = 12)),
  shapes = list(list(type = "line", xref = "paper", x0 = 0, x1 = 1,
    y0 = 100, y1 = 100, line = list(color = pal[["ink"]], width = 1, dash = "dot"))),
  annotations = list(
    list(xref = "paper", x = 0.99, y = 1.13, showarrow = FALSE,
      xanchor = "right", text = sprintf("deaths: %.2f to 1", season_ratio),
      font = list(size = 12, color = pal[["deaths"]])),
    list(xref = "paper", x = 0.99, y = 1.02, showarrow = FALSE,
      xanchor = "right", text = sprintf("events: %.2f to 1", ev_ratio),
      font = list(size = 12, color = pal[["events"]]))),
  xaxis = list(title = "", tickmode = "array", tickvals = 1:12,
    ticktext = month.abb, gridcolor = grid, zeroline = FALSE,
    tickfont = list(size = 12)),
  yaxis = list(title = "index, own mean = 100", gridcolor = grid,
    zeroline = FALSE, tickfont = list(size = 12)))

config(fig4, displayModeBar = FALSE)
```

*Pattern: the bars bow upward in the first half; the line does not move.*

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Where the numbers come from

**The file.** Kaggle `justtryit01/nigerian-insecurity-analysis-1997-2026`, MIT licence, compiled from
ACLED (1997–2026) and UCDP (1990–2024) via HDX. The version here is `acled_cleaned.csv`, filtered to
2015–2026 and committed as `data/acled_clean_lga_month.csv`: 106,536 rows, balanced, no duplicates, no
negatives. `data/PROVENANCE.md` records the source and the filter. 84.8 per cent of these LGA-months
record no events, which is why the trend model is a count model rather than a line through totals.

**The model.** One negative binomial with a state-varying slope, `pv_events ~ t + (1 + t | state)` on
the state-month panel, 37 × 132 rows, fitted with `glmmTMB`. The state estimate is the country slope
plus that state's conditional mode; the interval is the conditional standard deviation, so a small
state's trend is pulled toward the national one and a large state's is left alone. The national rate is
the fixed effect. `analysis.R` reproduces every number
here and caches the one fit that takes time; delete `cache/` to refit.

**"Worse", three ways.** A state is worse when its interval excludes zero: 33 states. Requiring
+10 per cent a year as well: 31. Applying Benjamini–Hochberg across the 37: 33. The post reports the
first; the other two are in `analysis.R`, because the list shrinking under a stricter rule is a fact
about the rule, not about Nigeria.

**The deadliest months.** Ranked on 2019–2025. 2026 is excluded deliberately: it holds six months, its
June is thin (131 events against May's 643), and ACLED revises recent months, so a 2026 month would win
or lose this table on reporting lag rather than on deaths.

**Caveats that belong here, not in a footnote.** ACLED coverage deepens over time, so 2015 and 2025 are
not the same reporting regime. Fatality counts in mass-casualty banditry are less reliable than event
counts. There is no population column, so "worse" is per area, not per capita. The file carries no
actors, event types, coordinates or exact dates, so "banditry against Borno" is not answerable from it.

**What this post does not do.** No forecast, no held-out score, no model comparison. The specification
for that work is `nigeria-conflict-methods-spec.md`; this post is the descriptive pass that comes before
it.
:::

::: {.aside-box .hommie}
> So the country is getting worse.

It is, and the average is the part that misleads. Borno carries one death in three and has barely moved since 2015. The fastest risers are small states with a fraction of its toll. Rank by speed and you get the north-west. Rank by deaths and you get Borno. Both lists are the country.
:::

## The formulas, said twice

Every number above comes out of one model. Here is the model, and here is what each line of it means.

::: {.dual}
::: {.spine}
$$\begin{aligned} Y_{st} &\sim \mathrm{NB}_2(\mu_{st},\theta)\\ \log \mu_{st} &= \alpha+\beta t+a_s+b_s t \end{aligned}$$
:::

::: {.dub}
Events in state $s$ and month $t$ are a negative binomial count — a Poisson whose variance is allowed to exceed its mean, which matters when a state has months of five events and months of five hundred. The log link keeps the fitted count positive.
:::

::: {.spine}
$$(a_s,b_s)\sim N(\mathbf 0,\Sigma)$$
:::

::: {.dub}
Each state gets its own level and its own trend, drawn from one distribution rather than estimated in isolation. That is what lets a small state borrow strength from the others, and it is why the state estimates are shrunk slightly toward the national line.
:::

::: {.spine}
$$\beta_s=\beta+b_s,\qquad 100\left(e^{\beta_s}-1\right)$$
:::

::: {.dub}
The percentage a year. A slope of $\beta_s$ on a log scale is a growth rate, and a growth rate only becomes a per cent change once it is exponentiated: +22.9 nationally, +59.8 in Sokoto, +8.9 in Borno.
:::

::: {.spine}
$$100\left(e^{\beta_s\,\pm\,1.96\,se_s}-1\right)$$
:::

::: {.dub}
The interval, on the same per cent scale — the horizontal lines in the first figure. A state counts as worse when the whole interval is right of zero, which is thirty-three of thirty-seven.
:::

::: {.spine}
$$\rho_S\big(\beta_s,\; D_s\big)=0.21$$
:::

::: {.dub}
Spearman's rank correlation between how fast a state is rising and how many deaths it has had. Almost none, which is the whole of the second section: the fastest states are not the deadliest states.
:::
:::
